title: Blocking a customer enforces nothing — no rule or Cloud Function ever reads isBlocked, and the Auth-disable failure is swallowed
detail: `adminBlockUser` writes `customers/{uid}.isBlocked = true` and then calls `auth.updateUser(uid, {disabled:true}).catch(() => undefined)` and `revokeRefreshTokens(...).catch(() => undefined)`. Every failure is swallowed, and the Firestore flag itself is enforced NOWHERE: `grep -rn isBlocked` over functions/, web/src, app/lib and firebase/firestore.rules returns only (a) this file, (b) the admin UI badge/label, (c) `request.resource.data.isBlocked == false` on customer *create* (firestore.rules:152), (d) the two clients writing `false` at signup. `placeOrder` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts), `executeSpin`, `topUpWallet`, `createReturnRequest`, `linkReferral` and the write rules for cart/addresses/reviews/wishlist contain no block check at all. So the ONLY enforcement is the Auth `disabled` flag — and seeded/imported customers (scripts/seed.ts:412 writes `customers/cust_001..008` with no `auth.createUser`) have no Firebase Auth record, so `updateUser` throws user-not-found, is caught, and the callable still returns `{ok:true}`.
failure_scenario: Admin opens /customers/cust_003 for a fraud account, clicks 'Block user', confirms. Toast says 'Yusuf Ali blocked' and the list badge flips to red 'Blocked'. Nothing happened: there is no Auth user to disable (error swallowed), no rule and no callable reads isBlocked, so the customer keeps placing COD orders, spending wallet balance, spinning and filing returns indefinitely. Even for a customer who does have an Auth user, an already-signed-in session keeps a valid ID token for up to an hour, and onCall does not check revocation, so checkout keeps working after the block.
fix: Add an `isBlocked` guard to the privileged customer callables (checkout/spin/topup/returns/linkReferral) and to the client-write rules (e.g. `get(/databases/$(database)/documents/customers/$(uid())).data.isBlocked == false` on cart/address/review writes). Stop swallowing the Auth errors: if `auth.updateUser` fails with anything other than user-not-found, throw so the admin sees the block did not take.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo and could not refute. (1) functions/src/customers/moderation.ts:28 does `auth.updateUser(uid,{disabled:true}).catch(()=>undefined)` and `revokeRefreshTokens(...).catch(()=>undefined)`, then returns {ok:true} — every failure is silent, so the admin toast lies whenever the Auth call fails. (2) A full-repo grep for `isBlocked` (excluding node_modules/dist/.next) returns ONLY: moderation.ts (writes), firestore.rules:161 (`request.resource.data.isBlocked == false` on customer CREATE — a write-shape constraint, not an access gate), packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:119 (type), admin UI badge/label (CustomerProfilePage.tsx, CustomersListPage.tsx), and web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:40 / scripts/seed.ts:428 / e2e returns.spec.ts:31 writing `false`. Zero hits in app/lib. (3) functions/src/_lib/guards.ts:28 `requireCustomer` is only `if (!req.auth) throw; return {uid}` — it never reads the customer doc, and all customer callables (placeOrder, applyCoupon, reserveStock, executeSpin, topUpWallet, createReturnRequest, linkReferral, affiliate requests) use it. firestore.rules has no blocked helper; cart/addresses/wishlist/reviews writes are isOwner-only. (4) No beforeUserSignedIn/beforeUserCreated blocking function exists in functions/src, and callableOpts (functions/src/_lib/admin.ts) adds no revocation check, so an existing ID token stays accepted by both rules and onCall for up to ~1h after a block. (5) scripts/seed.ts uses auth.createUser only in upsertAdmin (line 65); seedCustomers writes customers/cust_001..008 with no Auth record, so updateUser throws user-not-found, is swallowed, and nothing at all happens. Mitigation that softens but does not refute: real customers DO have Auth users (web/src/lib/otp/mockOtpService.ts uses createUserWithEmailAndPassword), so `disabled:true` does prevent future sign-in for them — the claim's 'enforces nothing' is overstated for that population, but the dead Firestore flag, the swallowed error, and the ≤1h live-session window are all real. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists; fix is straightforward (read isBlocked in requireCustomer, surface the Auth failure).

title: Wheel editor can never produce a `better_luck` slice — the "==" toggle silently means free_shipping
detail: `prizeTypeFor(kind, prev)` returns `prev === 'better_luck' ? 'better_luck' : 'free_shipping'` for the `special` kind. The row editor (CampaignDetailPage.tsx:431-444) renders exactly three buttons — `₹`, `%`, `==` — with no sub-choice between the two special prize types, and `newRow()` (CampaignDetailPage.tsx:103-118) always starts a row at `flat_discount`. Therefore clicking `==` on any newly added row always yields `free_shipping`, and there is no path in the UI to reach `better_luck` at all. `executeSpin` (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:129-132) classifies `free_shipping` as `isCoupon`, mints a real `customers/{uid}/coupons` doc with `discountType:'free_shipping'`, and `computeCouponDiscount` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:192-193, 331) sets `waiveDelivery = true` for it. The `==` glyph is also identical for both types, so an existing `better_luck` slice and a `free_shipping` slice are visually indistinguishable in the editor.
failure_scenario: Admin opens a campaign, deletes the starter "Better luck next time" row, clicks "Add offer", types "Better luck next time", clicks `==`, sets weight 40, and saves. The wheel now has a 40%-weighted slice labelled "Better luck next time" whose `prizeType` is `free_shipping`. Every customer who lands on the losing slice is issued a free-shipping coupon (app shows "You won!" via SpinOutcome, prizeType != 'better_luck'), and delivery is waived on their next order. The admin has no way to see or fix this from the editor.
fix: Split the `special` toggle into two explicit choices (e.g. a `🚚` free-shipping button and a `✕` better-luck button), or add a prize-type select for special slices. `prizeTypeFor` must be able to return `better_luck` from a non-better_luck previous value.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable defect; I could not refute it. prizeTypeFor(kind='special', prev) at admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:90 returns better_luck only when prev is already better_luck, and newRow() (admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx:103-118) always starts at flat_discount, so the three-button toggle (lines 431-444, the ONLY prizeType writer in all of admin/src — verified by grep) can never produce better_luck on a new row. Worse than reported: an EXISTING better_luck row is silently converted too — clicking ₹ then == runs prizeTypeFor('special','flat_discount') = free_shipping. Both special types render the identical '==' glyph, so the seeded campaign's s5 (better_luck) and s6 (free_shipping) at scripts/seed.ts:755-756 are indistinguishable in the editor. No downstream guard exists: functions/src/spin/execute.ts:129-132 treats free_shipping as isCoupon and mints a customers/{uid}/coupons doc, and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:191-193 + 347 force waiveDelivery/freeDelivery. better_luck is not a dead enum: web/src/app/(shop)/spin/result/page.tsx:27 uses prizeType !== 'better_luck' to decide "won", and app/lib/features/spin/spin_screen.dart:112 + spin_reward_screen.dart:99 render "SO CLOSE" vs "YOU WON". Also, validityDays is hidden for special rows, so a converted loss slice keeps validityDays 0 (seed) and mints an instantly-expired coupon. Not on the already-fixed list (which covers spin campaign expiry/broadcast counters, not slice prize types) nor on the known-intentional list. Only correction: the editor lives at admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx, not pages/; the cited line numbers match exactly.

title: No editor for `discountMaxCapPaise` / `minCartValuePaise` — every spin-won percent coupon is uncapped with no cart minimum
detail: `Row` carries `minCartValuePaise` and `discountMaxCapPaise` (lines 59-60) and `rowToSlice` writes them back (lines 92-93), but no input renders them — the row JSX (lines 424-520) has only the type toggle, label, value, validityDays, weight and delete. `newRow()` hardcodes `minCartValuePaise: 0, discountMaxCapPaise: null` (lines 112-113) and `starterSlices()` in api/spinner.ts:126 does the same. `executeSpin` copies both straight onto the issued coupon (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:165-166), and checkout honours them only when set: `const cap = Number(c.discountMaxCapPaise ?? 0); if (cap > 0) …` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:222-224) and `if (subtotalPaise < Number(c.minCartValuePaise ?? 0))` (checkout.ts:214). Worse, personal spin coupons are also auto-applied without the customer entering a code (`autoBestOffer`, checkout.ts:299-318). The label placeholder even advertises constraints the form cannot store: "Reward text (e.g. ₹10 off · min ₹99)" (line 452).
failure_scenario: Admin adds an offer, clicks `%`, types 50, labels it "50% off · min ₹999", weight 5, saves. A customer wins it, adds a ₹40,000 order to the cart, and checkout auto-applies the coupon with no cap and no minimum — ₹20,000 is deducted. The admin believed the '· min ₹999' text in the label constrained it; that text is purely cosmetic.
fix: Add "Min cart (₹)" and "Max discount (₹)" inputs to each non-special row, converting with `paiseFromRupees`, and require a cap on `percent` slices before allowing save.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable defect. The spin campaign editor (admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx) keeps minCartValuePaise/discountMaxCapPaise on Row (lines 59-60, self-described as "preserved (not surfaced in this editor)") and writes them back in rowToSlice (92-93), but renders no input for either; newRow() hardcodes 0/null (113-114) and starterSlices() in admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:126 does the same. CreateCampaignPage.tsx has no slice fields at all, so every slice an admin authors in the UI is permanently uncapped with no cart minimum (only scripts/seed.ts:751-756 contains real values, and they survive only via the round-trip). No backstop exists downstream: functions/src/spin/execute.ts:165-166 copies both fields onto the issued personal coupon verbatim, and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts treats absent as unlimited in all four sites (cap>0 guards at 199, 223, 292, 312; min-cart at 214 and 305). I grepped functions/src for any settings-level default cap and found none. autoBestOffer (checkout.ts:299-317) does apply personal spin coupons with no code entered, so the failure scenario needs no customer action. Refutation attempts all failed: the fields are authored only by the promotional coupon form (admin/src/features/coupons/routes/CouponFormPage.tsx); web/ and app/ merely read/format them; the route is registered at admin/src/app/router.tsx:84 so the path is reachable; and it is on neither the already-fixed nor known-intentional list. Decisively, CouponFormPage.tsx:132-133 hard-blocks saving a percent coupon without a cap ("A max-discount cap is required for percentage coupons."), so the spinner path can only ever produce exactly what the project's own rule forbids, with Math.min(discountPaise, eligiblePaise) as the sole limit (up to 100% of cart). The placeholder "Reward text (e.g. Rs.10 off, min Rs.99)" at line 452 is cosmetic but reinforces rather than refutes the claim.

title: No route-level permission gate: any sub-admin can read every customer's PII at /customers, because rules allow any admin to read the whole customers collection
detail: `/customers` and `/customers/:id` sit under `RequireAuth` only (RequireAuth.tsx checks a signed-in active admin, nothing else). Module permissions are applied purely cosmetically, in Sidebar.tsx:11-12 and dashboard QuickActions. firestore.rules:139 is `allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (isOwner(userId) || isAdmin())`, and `isAdmin()` is just `role == 'super_admin' || role == 'sub_admin'` (rules:12) — no module check. So the hiding is client-side only with no server enforcement.
failure_scenario: A sub-admin created with only reviews.view types /customers in the address bar. The nav item is hidden but the route renders: they get the full live list of every customer's name, phone, email, wallet balance and blocked status, and can open /customers/<uid> and click 'Export data' to download the whole customer document (addresses, bank accounts, cart) as JSON.
fix: Add a permission guard element around the module routes (e.g. `<RequireModule module="customers" action="view">`) redirecting to /, and tighten the rule to `can('customers','view')` for the non-owner branch of the customers read.

verdict.reason: Verified and could not refute. (1) /home/h/barkath/admin/src/app/router.tsx nests every route, including /customers and /customers/:id, under a single <RequireAuth/> + <AppShell/> pair with no per-route guard or loader. (2) /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx only waits for hydration and redirects when no admin is loaded — no module check. (3) A full grep of admin/src for modulePermissions shows only three functional consumers: Sidebar.tsx:12 (hides nav), QuickActions.tsx:42 (hides dashboard buttons), AccountDialogs.tsx:51 — i.e. purely cosmetic hiding. CustomersListPage.tsx and CustomerProfilePage.tsx contain zero permission checks, and CustomerProfilePage.tsx:98 onExportData serialises the entire customer doc to JSON unconditionally. (4) Server side does not re-check: firebase/firestore.rules:148 is `allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (isOwner(userId) || isAdmin())`, and isAdmin() (rules:12) is just role()=='super_admin' || role()=='sub_admin'. Crucially the rules DO define a per-module gate can(module,action)/canWrite(module) (rules:29-42, added per its own comment so a dashboard-only sub-admin could not rewrite the GST rate), but grepping shows can('...') is used exclusively on allow-write lines — can(module,'view') is never used anywhere, so no admin read is module-gated. (5) The scenario is reachable: emptyModulePermissions() in admin/src/features/subadmin/api/subadmin.ts:59 starts new sub-admins all-off, so a reviews-only sub-admin has customers.view=false yet still satisfies isAdmin(). (6) Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (which covers adminModerateReview for reviews-only sub-admins, not read gating) nor KNOWN-INTENTIONAL (App Check non-enforcement is a separate issue from isAdmin() lacking a module check). Only inaccuracies in the report are cosmetic: the rules line is 148 not 139, and RequireAuth does not itself verify 'active' status (that lives in the auth store). Systemic note: orders, supportTickets, reviews and the customer subcollections have the same isAdmin()-only read, but customers is the worst instance given the PII plus one-click full-document export.

title: Admin-granted spins (`spinsRemaining`) can never be spent — both customer surfaces disable the wheel on the daily cap alone
detail: "Grant spins" calls `adminGrantSpins` (admin/src/features/customers/api/customers.ts:63-70) which writes `customers/{uid}.spinsRemaining` (functions/src/spin/grant.ts:31). `executeSpin` treats that balance as bonus spins usable once the daily cap is exhausted (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:113-117, 122-125, 142). But neither customer surface reads `spinsRemaining`: the app computes `spinsLeftToday = spinsPerDay − usedToday` (app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:63-70) and gates `canSpin = hasData && spinsLeft > 0` (app/lib/features/spin/spin_screen.dart:231, 252), and the web does the same (web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:69-78) then sets `disabled={spinning || !campaign || spinsLeft <= 0}` (lines 189, 196). A grep for `spinsRemaining` across web/ and app/ finds only the customer-doc initialiser (web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:51, app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:247) — nothing ever reads it.
failure_scenario: A customer complains their spin failed. Admin opens the customer profile, types 5, clicks "Grant spins" and sees "Granted 5 spins · balance 5". The customer opens Spin & Win the same day after using their one daily spin: the button reads "No spins left" and is disabled on both the app and the web. The grant is unspendable and the admin card keeps showing "5 · Spins remaining (no daily reset)" forever.
fix: Have `spinsLeftToday` (app) and the `spinsLeft` memo (web) add `customers/{uid}.spinsRemaining` to the remaining daily allowance, mirroring `executeSpin`'s `exhaustedDaily || remaining > 0` logic.

verdict.reason: Real, fixable cross-surface defect; I could not refute it. adminGrantSpins (functions/src/spin/grant.ts:31) writes only customers/{uid}.spinsRemaining, and executeSpin (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:113-125,142) will honour that balance as a bonus spin once the daily cap is exhausted. But neither client ever reads the field: web computes spinsLeft = spinsPerDay − usedToday (web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:69-78) and both the wheel and button are disabled at spinsLeft <= 0 (lines 189,196), with an extra early return in spin() at line 137 so the callable is never even invoked; the Flutter app does the same (app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:56-70, app/lib/features/spin/spin_screen.dart:231,252). executeSpin has only those two callers. A repo-wide grep for spinsRemaining outside functions/admin/shared finds only the customer-doc initialisers and a now-stale e2e comment (e2e/tests/web/spin.spec.ts:8) that still claims the web count is the per-customer balance. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list — that pass fixed the server semantics only (execute.ts's own comment says the balance previously "gate[d] nothing at all"), leaving the clients unchanged. Not KNOWN-INTENTIONAL, not cosmetic, not unreachable: the admin's "Grant spins" action on admin/src/features/customers/routes/CustomerProfilePage.tsx:174 is a no-op for the customer, and the balance never decrements so the card shows it forever. Fix is viable client-side since firebase/firestore.rules:139 allows the owner to read their own customer doc.

title: `rewardCouponExpiryDays` hardcoded to 7 with no editor, yet the app shows it to customers as the coupon validity
detail: `createCampaign` hardcodes `rewardCouponExpiryDays: 7` (line 150) and `saveCampaign` (lines 170-178) never writes it, so no admin control can ever change it. The app reads it and renders it verbatim under the wheel — `'Rewards become coupons · valid ${campaign.rewardCouponExpiryDays} days · one per order'` (app/lib/features/spin/spin_screen.dart:257) — and uses it as the expiry fallback in the reward sheet (spin_screen.dart:120). The value that actually governs expiry is the *per-slice* `validityDays` the admin DOES edit (CampaignDetailPage.tsx:476-487 → functions/src/spin/execute.ts:155-156). The seed writes 3 (scripts/seed.ts:761), so seeded and admin-created campaigns disagree.
failure_scenario: Admin sets every slice's validity to 30 days in the wheel editor and saves. The app's Spin & Win screen still tells the customer "Rewards become coupons · valid 7 days", because `rewardCouponExpiryDays` is stuck at the hardcoded 7 the create form wrote. Set a slice to 3 days instead and the banner over-promises 7 days on a coupon that expires in 3.
fix: Either surface `rewardCouponExpiryDays` as a campaign-level field in the settings card and have `saveCampaign` persist it, or drop it from the doc and have the app derive the banner from the slices' `validityDays` range.

verdict.reason:
Could not refute — every load-bearing fact checks out.

1. Hardcoded, never editable. `rewardCouponExpiryDays` appears in exactly three places in the whole repo (grep across admin/, web/, app/, functions/, packages/, scripts/): the type at /home/h/barkath/packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:108, the hardcoded write at /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:150 (`rewardCouponExpiryDays: 7`), and the seed at /home/h/barkath/scripts/seed.ts:761 (`3`). `saveCampaign` (spinner.ts:163-181) writes name/slices/eligibility/spinsPerDay/startsAt/endsAt/updatedAt only. Grepping /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner for "expiry" matches only line 150 plus one unrelated comment — there is no input, no label, no display of this field anywhere in the admin (files confirmed: routes/CreateCampaignPage.tsx, routes/SpinnerListPage.tsx, routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx, api/spinner.ts). So no admin action can ever change it, and nothing server-side recomputes or overwrites it.

2. The app really does render it verbatim to customers. /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/spin/spin_screen.dart:257 — `'Rewards become coupons · valid ${campaign.rewardCouponExpiryDays} days · one per order'` — unconditional, no fallback, directly under the Spin button. Parsed at app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_campaign.dart:91-92 with its own default of 3 (which also disagrees with the admin's 7 for any campaign missing the field).

3. It is not the value that governs expiry. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/spin/execute.ts:155-156 computes `const days = Number(slice.validityDays ?? 30); const expiresAt = ...` — the per-slice `validityDays`, which the admin DOES edit (CampaignDetailPage.tsx:481-482, path corrected from the claim's `pages/` to `routes/`). So the campaign-level field and the actual coupon expiry are fully decoupled.

Net: an admin who sets slice validity to 3 or 30 days still ships a banner promising "valid 7 days". That is a wrong, customer-visible commercial promise sourced from an admin-owned field the admin cannot reach — a genuine cross-surface mismatch, not cosmetic polish, and fixable either by exposing an editor or by deriving the banner from the slices.

Two small corrections to the claim, neither of which weakens it: the admin file lives at admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx (not pages/), and the second app usage (spin_screen.dart:120, `slice?.validityDays ?? campaign.rewardCouponExpiryDays`) is a correct-by-precedence fallback that only misfires if a slice lacks validityDays — the real bite is line 257. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (which covers only spin campaign *expiry computed on read* and broadcast opens) nor the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list.

title: `SpinSlice.usedCount` is never incremented by any writer, and the editor's help text promises a Usage column that does not exist
detail: The editor copy reads "…then set a probability weight — the wheel splits by relative weight. **Usage shows how many players landed on it.**" (lines 408-411), but no usage cell is rendered anywhere in the row JSX (lines 424-520). `usedCount` is read into `Row` (line 76) and written straight back on save (line 99, api/spinner.ts:126). Grepping every surface, the only writers of `usedCount` are `scripts/seed.ts:751-756` (static fake numbers 120/40/22/8/200/30) and this round-trip; `functions/src/spin/execute.ts` increments only `totalSpins` and `totalCouponsIssued` (lines 193-196) and never touches the slice's counter. So on a real campaign every slice's `usedCount` is 0 forever, and on the seeded campaign it is frozen fake data.
failure_scenario: Admin reads "Usage shows how many players landed on it", looks for the per-slice usage numbers to rebalance the wheel, and finds no such column. If they instead inspect the Firestore doc (or a future report is built on the field), the seeded campaign reports 200 hits on "Better luck" and 120 on "₹10 off" — numbers that came from the seed script and have not moved after thousands of real spins.
fix: Increment the winning slice's `usedCount` inside the `executeSpin` transaction (read-modify-write on the `slices` array alongside the existing `campRef` update), then render a Usage column per row — or delete both the field and the sentence.

verdict.reason: Verified and not refutable. CampaignDetailPage.tsx:408-411 tells the admin "Usage shows how many players landed on it", but the row JSX (424-520: type toggle, label, value, validity days, weight/chance bar, delete) renders no usage cell, and grep for "usage" across admin/src/features/spinner returns only that one copy line. usedCount has no writer anywhere: the only occurrences repo-wide are the shared type (packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:96), the admin read/write round-trip (CampaignDetailPage.tsx:76,99,112 and api/spinner.ts:126 starter slices at 0), and static seed values (scripts/seed.ts:751-756). functions/src/spin/execute.ts writes a spinHistory doc carrying sliceId and updates the campaign with only totalSpins/totalCouponsIssued increments; it never rewrites the slices array, so usedCount is 0 forever on any real campaign. No compute-on-read fallback exists either -- api/spinner.ts derives only effectiveSpinStatus and campaign-level conversionPct, and no admin surface aggregates spinHistory by sliceId. Not on the already-fixed list (which covers spin campaign expiry compute-on-read and broadcasts.opened, not slice counters) or the intentional list. The claim does overreach on one point: the stale seeded numbers are not user-visible since nothing renders usedCount, so that part of the failure scenario is weak. The surviving defect is the misleading editor copy backed by a permanently dead schema field -- low severity but real and fixable (drop the sentence, or wire a counter/aggregation from spinHistory.sliceId).

title: Profile tabs ignore loading and error from their queries — a failed query renders a permanent, wrong empty state
detail: `AffiliateTab` (line 386), `WalletTab` (line 290) and `OrdersTab` (line 256) each destructure only `{ data }` from the hooks, discarding the `loading` and `error` fields that `useLiveCollection` returns (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets `{data: previous, loading:false, error}` on failure). The commissions query is `where('affiliateUid','==',uid) + orderBy('accruedAt','desc')` (customers.ts:46), which needs the composite index in firebase/firestore.indexes.json:50 — if that index is missing in an environment, or if rules deny the read, the tab renders 'No affiliate earnings yet.' forever with the FirestoreError only in the console.
failure_scenario: Admin opens a top affiliate's profile → 'Affiliate wallet' tab. The header shows ₹3,200 confirmed balance (read from the customer doc) but the table says 'No affiliate earnings yet.' because the commissions listener failed with failed-precondition (index) or permission-denied. The admin concludes the commissions were never accrued. The same tab also flashes the empty state for a beat on every open, even on success.
fix: Read `loading`/`error` in all three tabs: render a spinner while `loading && data.length===0`, and an explicit error row ('Couldn't load commissions — retry') when `error` is set.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code and not refutable. OrdersTab (CustomerProfilePage.tsx:256), WalletTab (:290) and AffiliateTab (:386) each destructure only `{ data }` from useLiveCollection, which returns `{data, loading, error}` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:99-121; the error callback sets `{data: previous, loading:false, error}`). Tabs mount lazily (lines 216-218), so every first click on a tab starts a cold cache entry (`loading:true, data:[]`) and renders 'No orders yet.' / 'No wallet activity.' / 'No affiliate earnings yet.' for the whole round trip — the exact empty-state flash the cache's docstring was written to prevent — and any listener error leaves that wrong empty state permanently with only a console FirestoreError. This is a deviation from the established house pattern, not the house pattern: SubAdminListPage.tsx:123-127 renders an explicit 'Loading…' row then a 'Couldn't load admins. Please try again.' error row, and OrdersListPage:117, PaymentsListPage:100, InventoryListPage:109, AdjustStockPage:133 all guard with `loading && rows.length === 0`; CouponsListPage, ReturnsListPage, BannerListPage, NotificationsListPage and SpinnerListPage all read `error`. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Two corrections to the claim, which is why confidence is medium rather than high: (1) the commissions composite index (affiliateUid ASC + accruedAt DESC) IS declared in firebase/firestore.indexes.json (~line 72, not line 50), so failed-precondition only occurs in an environment where indexes were not deployed; (2) permission-denied is unlikely for the admin panel since firestore.rules:110-113 grants the read to any isAdmin() (super_admin or sub_admin) with no module gate. Also the OrdersTab query is equality-only (customers.ts:31) and needs no composite index, so the error half of the claim is weak there. The unconditional, always-reproducible half is the missing loading guard.

title: Customers list renders 'No customers yet.' when the Firestore query fails
detail: The page takes `{ data: customers, loading }` and drops `error` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117 sets `loading:false, error` on the snapshot error path). The empty branch at line 112-114 therefore prints 'No customers yet.' for a permission-denied / unavailable / index error, and the header at line 74 confidently prints '0 registered · 0 affiliates'.
failure_scenario: Rules are redeployed with the customers read tightened, or the admin's session loses its role claim. Every admin opening /customers sees a clean 'No customers yet.' and a '0 registered' header, and reports that the customer database was wiped; the actual permission-denied error is silently swallowed.
fix: Surface `error` from `useCustomersList()` as a distinct error state ('Couldn't load customers') and keep the count header blank while erroring.

verdict.reason: Claim verified. CustomersListPage.tsx:19 destructures only {data, loading} from useCustomersList(); the two 'error' tokens in the file are toast.error calls in the affiliate-toggle handler, not the read path. firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets {data: previous ([] on first attach), loading:false, error} on the snapshot error callback, so a permission-denied read exits the loading branch at line 108 and falls into line 113 printing 'No customers yet.', with the header at line 74 asserting '0 registered · 0 affiliates'. Nothing else surfaces the error: the hook does not toast/log/throw, and there is no ErrorBoundary anywhere in admin/src (grep for ErrorBoundary|componentDidCatch returns nothing). The path is reachable: RequireAuth.tsx gates on the admins doc in the auth store, while firestore.rules:157 (allow read: isOwner(userId) || isAdmin()) evaluates request.auth.token.role, so a stale/missing role claim denies the read while the page still renders. Not on the already-fixed list ('auth listener has an error path' refers to the authStore listener, not collection subscriptions) and not on the known-intentional list. Not cosmetic — the page asserts a false fact ('0 registered') rather than just looking odd. The codebase's own convention confirms this is treated as a defect elsewhere: BannerListPage.tsx:77-78, CouponsListPage.tsx:124-126, plus spinner, returns, subadmin, notifications, reviews and products list pages all consume the same hook's error and render an error row; customers (with orders and payments) is the anomaly. Severity is moderate (misleading state, not data loss) and the fix is a small error branch mirroring CouponsListPage.tsx:124.

title: "Activate" on an expired campaign reports success but leaves it dead
detail: `onToggleStatus` reads `loadedRef.current.status`, which is the *effective* status from `useSpinCampaign` → `withEffectiveStatus` (api/spinner.ts:42-45, 60-64). For a campaign past `endsAt` this is `'ended'`, so `isActive` is false, the button renders "Activate", and clicking it writes `status:'active'` and toasts "Campaign activated" (lines 256-260). But `effectiveSpinStatus` immediately recomputes `'ended'` from the unchanged `endsAt`, so the badge flips straight back; `executeSpin` still rejects with "This spin campaign has ended." (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:62, checked *before* status) and both the app (spin_repository.dart:39-46) and admin list keep hiding it.
failure_scenario: Admin opens a campaign that ended yesterday, sees the "Activate" button, clicks it, gets a green "Campaign activated" toast — and nothing changes. No customer can spin, and the admin is never told that the end date is the blocker.
fix: Disable the button (or relabel it "Extend & activate") when `effectiveSpinStatus(campaign) === 'ended'`, and either refuse the write or push `endsAt` forward as part of the same action.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Verified end to end:

1. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:36-45 — `effectiveSpinStatus` returns 'ended' when `status === 'active'` and `endsAt < now`; `withEffectiveStatus` is applied by BOTH `useSpinCampaignsList` (60-64) and `useSpinCampaign` (73-78). So the detail page receives the *derived* status, not the stored one.

2. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx:141 — `loadedRef.current = campaign` stores that same derived object; line 256 `const next = loaded.status === 'active' ? 'paused' : 'active'` and line 286 `const isActive = campaign.status === 'active'` therefore both read the derived value. For a campaign past `endsAt` the button renders "Activate" (line 297) and clicking writes `{status:'active'}` via `setCampaignStatus` (api/spinner.ts:181) then toasts "Campaign activated" (line 260) unconditionally on write success. There is no `endsAt` guard, no `disabled`, and the write is a literal no-op when the stored status is already 'active' (only `updatedAt` moves). Checked the exclusion lists: the ALREADY-FIXED entry "Spin campaign expiry computed on read" is precisely what introduced this asymmetry (the read is window-aware, the write path is not), so it does not cover this. Reachable, real, and fixable (guard on `endsAt`/use the stored status for the toggle and prompt to extend the window).

title: Nothing prevents multiple simultaneously-active campaigns; the web picks an arbitrary one and ignores the schedule window
detail: Neither `createCampaign` (api/spinner.ts:139-160, with "Activate immediately" defaulting to `true` at CreateCampaignPage.tsx:33) nor `setCampaignStatus` (api/spinner.ts:181) deactivates any other campaign, and the list page happily shows several "Active" cards. The web reads `query(collection(db,'spinCampaigns'), where('status','==','active'))` with no `orderBy` and no window filter, then takes `campaigns.data[0]` (lines 54-58). The app is stricter — it filters `startsAt…endsAt` in `_isLive` (app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:39-46) — so the two surfaces can serve different campaigns, and the web can serve a scheduled-but-not-started or already-ended one.
failure_scenario: Admin creates "Eid Mega Spin" starting next month with "Activate immediately" left on (the default), while "Ramadan Spin" is still running. On the web rewards page the customer may be shown the Eid wheel (Firestore returns it first), and every click on Spin returns `failed-precondition: This spin campaign hasn't started yet.` — while the app correctly shows the Ramadan wheel. In the admin the new campaign shows the badge "Scheduled", giving no hint it is live to web users.
fix: Enforce single-active in the admin (deactivate other campaigns when one is activated, or block activation with a clear error), and add the `startsAt/endsAt` window filter + a deterministic sort to the web query so it matches the app and `executeSpin`.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading all four surfaces. web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:54-58 queries spinCampaigns with only where('status','==','active'), no orderBy, no window filter, and takes campaigns.data[0]; useCollection (web/src/lib/useCollection.ts) applies no sorting, so the pick is arbitrary (__name__ order). No later guard in the file checks startsAt/endsAt — spin() only guards !campaign and spinsLeft<=0, and its catch handles only 'resource-exhausted', so a 'failed-precondition' window rejection surfaces as the generic WALLET_CF_MSG toast. This is the only spinCampaigns read in web/. By contrast app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:26-46 does filter the window in _isLive, with a doc comment stating "status alone is not enough: nothing ever flips it when the campaign's window opens/closes" — so the surfaces provably diverge. functions/src/spin/execute.ts:56-64 checks the window before status and throws the exact "This spin campaign hasn't started yet." message; it rejects rather than falling back. On the admin side, createCampaign (admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:139-160) writes status:'active' when activateImmediately and setCampaignStatus (line 181) is a bare single-doc updateDoc — neither deactivates siblings, and firestore.rules:61 is a plain canWrite('spinnerCampaigns') with no uniqueness enforcement. CreateCampaignPage.tsx:33 is useState(true), so "Activate immediately" is the default, with editable dates defaulting to today→+30d. effectiveSpinStatus/statusBadge compute 'ended'/'Scheduled' on read but live only in admin/ and are never imported by web. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list: the compute-on-read spin-expiry fix reached admin, app and the callable but skipped the web rewards page, and the stated architecture rule (campaign expiry is compute-on-read, sweeps best-effort) makes an unfiltered status=='active' read a genuine violation. Impact is functional, not cosmetic: wrong slices rendered and every spin dead-ends in a generic error. Only minor overstatement is that the admin does badge a future campaign "Scheduled" — but that badge is admin-local and does not prevent the web from serving it.

title: "Activate immediately" publishes the hardcoded starter wheel before the admin has configured anything
detail: `createCampaign` writes `status:'active'` when the toggle is on — and it defaults to on (CreateCampaignPage.tsx:33) — together with `starterSlices()`: a hardcoded `₹10 off` / `10% off` / `Better luck next time` wheel (api/spinner.ts:125-132) with weights 40/30/30 and `minCartValuePaise: 0`. The doc is live to customers the instant it is written (app spin_repository.dart:26-35 streams `status=='active'` and `startsAt` is set to today 00:00), i.e. before the admin has reached the wheel editor that the success toast ("Campaign created — configure the wheel") tells them to go configure.
failure_scenario: Admin fills in the name "Eid Mega Spin", leaves the defaults, clicks "Create & configure". Between that click and finishing the wheel editor, customers on the app can already spin and win real ₹10-off and uncapped 10%-off coupons from a placeholder wheel the admin never chose.
fix: Always create as `draft`, and move activation to the detail page after the wheel is saved (or default the "Activate immediately" toggle to off and only allow it once slices are configured).

verdict.reason:
Could not refute — every link in the chain checks out, and no guard, fallback or server re-check exists.

1. Write side (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:139-160): `createCampaign` writes `status: v.activateImmediately ? 'active' : 'draft'`, `startsAt = new Date(`${startDate}T00:00:00`)` and `slices: starterSlices()` in one `setDoc`. `starterSlices()` (lines 125-132) is a hardcoded placeholder wheel: `₹10 off` (flat 1000 paise, weight 40), `10% off` (weight 30, `discountMaxCapPaise: null`, i.e. UNCAPPED), `Better luck next time` (weight 30), all with `minCartValuePaise: 0`, `validityDays: 7`.

2. Default is on: /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CreateCampaignPage.tsx:33 `const [activate, setActivate] = useState(true)` and line 29 `startDate = isoDate(today)`, so `startsAt` is today 00:00 — already in the past. `onCreate` (37-70) does only name/date validation, then writes and toasts "Campaign created — configure the wheel", i.e. the flow itself admits the wheel is not configured yet.

3. It is immediately visible to customers on both surfaces: app `/home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:26-35` streams `where('status', isEqualTo: 'active')` and `_isLive()` only checks the startsAt/endsAt window (both satisfied); web `/home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:54-58` does `query(collection(db,'spinCampaigns'), where('status','==','active'))` and takes `campaigns.data[0]`. Rules (/home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.rules:61) allow any signed-in user to read spinCampaigns.

4. Server-side does NOT re-check configuration: /home/h/barkath/functions/src/spin/execute.ts validates window, `camp.status !== 'active'`, `slices.length === 0`, and eligibility — the starter slices satisfy all of them — then issues a real `customers/{uid}/coupons` doc with `discountMaxCapPaise: null`, `minCartValuePaise: 0`, `status: 'active'`. So a customer really can win an uncapped 10%-off coupon from a wheel the admin never chose.

5. Nothing reverts it: `CampaignDetailPage.tsx` only pauses/activates on an explicit click (line 256) and saves slices on explicit save (line 237); there is no create-time draft downgrade. The claim is not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (only "Spin campaign expiry computed on read" touches this feature) nor on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list.

Only nuance worth noting: `starterSlices()` is deliberate scaffolding ("so a freshly-created campaign is already configurable"), so the defect is really the combination of it with `activate` defaulting to `true` — the fix is either defaulting the toggle off, forcing `draft` until the wheel is saved, or making the starter prizes non-issuing (weight 0 / better_luck only). Either way it is a real, cheaply fixable defect with actual financial exposure.

title: `executeSpin` reads the customer's entire `spinHistory` on every spin (unbounded, grows forever)
detail: `db.collection('spinHistory').where('customerId','==',uid).get()` fetches every spin the customer has ever taken — across all campaigns, all time — then filters to today's campaign in memory (lines 103-108). There is no `createdAt` bound and no `limit`. The same unbounded pattern is mirrored client-side by live listeners: web `query(collection(db,'spinHistory'), where('customerId','==',uid))` (web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:61-64) and app `_history` (app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:47-52), both `snapshots()`/live with no bound.
failure_scenario: A daily-spinner customer after a year has ~365 `spinHistory` docs; each spin costs a 365-doc read server-side plus a 365-doc realtime listener on the client, and both grow without limit. Nothing in the admin ever prunes `spinHistory` (no admin surface reads or writes that collection at all).
fix: Add `.where('campaignId','==',campaignId).where('createdAt','>=', Timestamp.fromMillis(istMidnightMs))` with the composite index (or store a per-day counter doc such as `customers/{uid}/spinCounters/{campaignId}_{yyyymmdd}`), and bound the client listeners the same way.

verdict.reason: Verified accurate at /home/h/barkath/functions/src/spin/execute.ts:103: `db.collection('spinHistory').where('customerId','==',uid).get()` has no limit, no createdAt bound, and no campaignId filter — it reads the customer's entire lifetime spin history on every spin and filters to today's campaign in memory (lines 104-108). The inline comment (94-99) only justifies running the query outside the transaction and avoiding a composite index; it never claims the read is bounded, and firebase/firestore.indexes.json shows composite indexes are routinely added for orders/commissions, so the index argument is a choice, not a constraint. No mitigation exists elsewhere: functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts (the only scheduled file) never touches spinHistory, firestore.rules sets `allow write: if false` on it, and repo-wide the only readers are the two client listeners, which mirror the same unbounded pattern as live subscriptions (web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:60-63 and app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:47-52). Nothing ever prunes the collection. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (the prior spin finding in audit/findings.json is the unrelated spinsRemaining gating bug, which is already fixed in the current file) nor on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list. Severity is modest — growth is linear per-customer (~365 docs/year for a daily spinner), so it is a cost/latency scalability defect rather than a correctness break — but it is real and cheaply fixable by adding a createdAt >= IST-midnight bound (or orderBy+limit) plus the matching composite index, mirrored in both clients. Confidence is medium only because the impact is bounded per-user rather than catastrophic.
